public_rationale: The evidence supports significant limitations in tested language models and video generators. Simulation research also shows meaningful successes. The retrieved studies do not establish the full three-approach claim as of January 2025, particularly its simulation component. Nor do the successful specialized systems contradict the ordinary reading that no broad solution had been demonstrated.
limitations: Partial support for two approaches is insufficient to score the entire conjunction supported.
An old benchmark's failures cannot establish the contemporary limits of a whole approach.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: None of the three popular approaches to commonsense reasoning (simulation, LLM emergence, video generation) has proved fully satisfactory.

statement.excerpt: Three approaches to commonsense reasoning have become popular in the last fifteen years; none has proved fully satisfactory.
statement.document_title: AI still lacks “common” sense, 70 years later

our_interpretation: The three approaches are physical simulation, commonsense emerging in foundation models, and video generation.
'Fully satisfactory' means demonstrated, broadly reliable commonsense reasoning across ordinary situations. It does not require error-free performance.
The stated fifteen-year interval ends on the post date.
Success on a restricted task is relevant progress but does not by itself settle whether an entire approach has supplied a broad solution.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes material unresolved scope or reliability limits for all three approaches as of the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one approach has demonstrated broadly reliable commonsense reasoning by the post date.

evidence.explanation: The tested language models have substantial spatial-reasoning weaknesses, supporting the foundation-model part. The paper also reports improvements with scale and fine-tuning; available_at conservatively uses the end of the stated publication month.
PhyGenBench finds physical-consistency failures across its tested video generators. This supports the video-generation part, within the models and physical laws tested.

This establishes historical difficulty in a simulated physical-reasoning environment. It does not establish that simulation-based reasoning remained broadly inadequate five years later, or that the simulator itself was the failing component.

The model infers hidden fluid properties and transfers them to new simulated scenes. This is meaningful progress under incomplete physical information, but its restricted task scope does not establish a general commonsense solution.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A contemporaneous synthesis or reproducible evaluations covering leading systems in all three approaches, with explicit evidence about broad reliability and generalization.
